title: Sovereign Citizens: "The Classroom Lecture" by Joe The Lawyer
summary: A lawyer's continuing-education lecture on sovereign citizens: origins, core theories, Moorish offshoots, courtroom and traffic-stop tactics, psychology and why they fail.

assertions.quote: in the 1970s there was a movement called the posse comitatus movement and the founder his name is william p gail
in their minds nobody has authority or jurisdiction over them unless they have literally consented to it

verdicts.note: Jurisdiction comes from law and territory, not consent; courts routinely reject 'I do not consent' arguments.

assertions.quote: they think if there's a gold fringe flag in a courtroom it means that's a corporate courtroom

verdicts.note: Flag fringe is decorative; courts have repeatedly held it has no bearing on jurisdiction.

assertions.quote: they say because of this treaty your laws the laws of the united states of america do not apply to me
once automobiles were created states passed laws requiring people to drive with the license

verdicts.note: Courts recognise a right to interstate travel but uniformly hold that states may require licences to drive on public roads.

assertions.quote: they will file liens against judges they'll file liens against attorneys
there are multiple accounts of sovereign citizens killing or shooting police officers
they play lawyer they sell fake legal documents online they sell fake subscriptions online
if i can say anything is it it will not help the jail sentence

verdicts.note: Judges and practitioners report lost mitigation, contempt findings, sanctions and harsher outcomes; systematic data is limited.

assertions.quote: they'll beat a case for a different reason like they'll be offered a deal or something

verdicts.note: Reported 'wins' trace to dismissals, plea deals, missing officers or procedural errors, not acceptance of the theory.

assertions.quote: they borrow pieces of the american and british movement and uh you know combine it with their own ideas
they will go into abandoned houses and claim them as their own
